result.headline: Longitudinal control fault: pitch moves opposite its setpoint twice, with airspeed reading a constant 0 all flight.
result.explanation: Pitch/throttle (energy) control lost authority at 1-7 s and 153-160 s, with airspeed stuck at 0. A missing or failed airspeed input is the leading area, not confirmed. Roll tracking looks healthy.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (1983 samples)
evidence.shows: Airspeed never reads anything but 0 for 162 s, so the controller had no usable airspeed.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.961 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor-health error was raised at the start of the flight, alongside a low-voltage warning. The sensor is not named.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=0.899 to 6.757 s (peak |error| 46.115 deg)
evidence.shows: Pitch went to about +22 deg while the setpoint was about -23 deg. The response was opposite to the command.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=153.527 to 160.16 s (peak |error| 37.991 deg)
evidence.shows: The same opposite-pitch pattern repeats at the end, with throttle cut from 47 to 26 %.

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[roll] vs vehicle.attitude[roll]: typical |error| 4.72 deg, worst 56.857 at t=20.666 s; 6 window(s) above 14.161
evidence.shows: Roll follows its setpoint well overall, so the fault is mainly longitudinal.

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline in 0-10 s and 0-40 s
checked.result: No series left baseline in order; only the two start events at 0.961 s. The fault is already present at the start of the recording, so the earliest sign cannot be found.

checked.check: Sequence at the late event, 150-162 s
checked.result: ch3 and ch4 left baseline at 152.713 s, then the pitch setpoint at 153.356, ch2 at 153.365, throttle at 153.374, altitude at 154.216 and pitch attitude at 154.731 s. The commands led and the vehicle followed.

checked.check: Throttle against ch2 and pitch setpoint against ch2
checked.result: Correlations were 0.998 and 0.955 at zero lag. ch2 is the throttle/motor output, and the throttle command follows the pitch setpoint, as in energy-based control.
Correlation -0.199. The channel mapping is unclear, but roll attitude tracks its setpoint (line 75). Roll is not clearly faulty.

checked.check: Window 0-10 s of altitude, throttle, pitch and airspeed
checked.result: Throttle fell to 4 % at about 4 s while pitch was +22 deg against a -24 deg setpoint. Altitude fell from 78 to 47 m with airspeed 0. This looks like a stall or energy loss, not a sensor jump.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.altitude[relative] at t=4.634 s: 71.847 -> 50.511 m (step -21.337, 119.2x its usual variation)
effects.why: This is a sampling-gap artifact of a continuous descent (78 to 47 m over about 7 s), so it is a consequence of the pitch/throttle excursion.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=27.135 s: -513.249 -> -615.156 deg (step -101.907, 164.6x its usual variation)
effects.why: The yaw values exceed 360 deg and yaw rate is constant 0. This looks like an unwrapped or unrecorded yaw signal, not an independent fault.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.velocity[x] at t=11.883 s: 18.2 -> -10.07 m/s (step -28.27, 134.6x its usual variation)
effects.why: Velocity swings follow the large roll manoeuvres, so they are consequences of the manoeuvres.

outcomes.label: Airspeed stays 0 under blowing
outcomes.means: Pitot, wiring or the airspeed sensor configuration is dead or disabled, which fits the sensor-health error.
outcomes.then: Inspect sensor wiring and parameters, then test the elevator direction.

outcomes.label: Airspeed rises when blown
outcomes.means: The sensor works on the bench. Look at flight-time wiring, a logging issue, or the pitch control path.
outcomes.then: Run a ground test of elevator direction against pitch command.

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed is missing or dead, so energy and pitch control had no airspeed and lost authority.
hypotheses.because: Airspeed is a constant 0 for 1983 samples, a sensor-health error is raised at start, and the pitch excursions fit lost airspeed. Not directly tested.

hypotheses.claim: Elevator direction or authority is wrong, so pitch moves opposite its command.
hypotheses.because: Pitch moves opposite its setpoint at 1-7 s and 153-160 s. Commanded outputs were not compared with surface position.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage degraded the thrust available or triggered the health warnings.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning is raised at 0.961 s, but there is no voltage series. Throttle reached 60 % or more without an obvious limit.

hypotheses.claim: The roll control path is faulty.
hypotheses.because: Roll tracking error is typically 4.72 deg, with only brief divergences. The ch1 mapping to roll is unclear.

hypotheses.claim: The yaw or altitude estimate is corrupt and misleads the controller.
hypotheses.because: The altitude step is a sampling-gap artifact of a real descent. The yaw anomalies look like unwrapped angle or unrecorded yaw rate.

events.why: Unconfirmed; no voltage series is available to check it.

events.what: Sensor health error and airspeed constant 0
events.why: The controller had no usable airspeed during the flight.

events.what: Pitch diverges opposite to setpoint, twice
events.why: This is the visible control fault, in the longitudinal axis.

events.what: Altitude and pitch steps during the episodes
events.why: These follow the pitch and throttle excursions.

events.what: Constant outputs on ch0, ch6, ch7 and yaw rate
events.why: Unused channels or an unrecorded signal; no sign of a fault.
